_README: TBSLICE config: the campaign-readiness slice Requirement 9.6 is measured and cited
against. It exists to prove the Testbench_Agent's input-window alignment rule (and the
coverage-gap closure) on real RTLLM problems, not just on the one problem
(rtllm/arithmetic/accu) that motivated the rule. One arm, 15 designs spanning
arithmetic, control, memory, and miscellaneous, one sample each = 15 sessions.
node --env-file=.env app/eval/dist/sweep/cli.js --config app/eval/sweep/sweep.config.tbslice.json
HOW THIS SLICE IS CITED (Requirement 9.6, 9.7): run this exact config, take the
instrument-valid sample count from the summary, then diff it against the count from an
earlier run of this SAME file before the input-alignment rule (task 7.1) landed. The two
runs are directly comparable only because this file's Config_Identity hash is unchanged
by that prompt change - what moves the hash instead is TESTBENCH_PROMPT_VERSION
(app/agent/roles/testbench/prompt-version.ts), which config-identity.ts folds into the
canonical JSON directly from the running code, not from any field in this file. So a
result produced under one prompt version can never silently pool with one produced
under another.
The credential NEVER goes in this file. It comes from the environment (.env).
ARTIFACTS: on by default, written to .eval-runs/tbslice-v1/artifacts/. Note that samples
already in results.jsonl are SKIPPED on a re-run, so a sample recorded before artifacts
existed will not grow them retroactively. To capture evidence for those, run into a
fresh outputDir/runName.
_problems: 15 real, spelling-verified RTLLM designs (checked against the pinned checkout on disk
and against .eval-corpus/rtllm/File_list.md), spanning all three categories named by
adder_pipe_64bit, multi_16bit, multi_pipe_8bit, multi_booth_8bit, div_16bit), 3 control
(signal_generator, calendar, traffic_light). None is rtllm/arithmetic/accu or a
neighbour of it, and none is one of the four Stage 0 quarantined designs
